text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Aviation minister Air Commodore Ita Udoh Umeh heads inspection team visiting airlines to determine airworthiness of their fleet following a spate of air accidents since November.

- Special vessel to deliver liquefied petroleum gas from the midwestern site of the Escravos Gas Project, a joint venture between multinational Chevron Nigeria and state oil company NNPC, to arrive in March.

- Construction of gas transmission system (GTS) for the liquefied natural gas (LNG) plant, to transport gas from the fields to the site in southeastern Bonny town, will be completed within 17 months, the Nigeria LNG company says.
- Row erupts in oil-producing midwestern Warri town over which group of persons has right to negotiate development issues with oil multinationals operating there.
- Police in eastern Enugu town detain 17 lecturers for allegedly triggering last month's students unrest in nearby University of Nigeria, Nsukka.
- Seven-man trade delegation from Malaysia visits oil-producing Bayelsa state in the southeast to assess prospects for a palmoil processing company there.
- Police arrest and detain Joseph Wayas, Senate president between 1979 and 1983, for undisclosed reason.
